comment: Hand-written notes on whether hunting is allowed on public land, by managing body or by site. The first note is different: it applies to any site the source data lists as closed to the public, whoever manages it. See docs/DECISIONS.md D16. Each note cites a public rule or page. The first matching note wins, so site notes come before manager notes. Matching is case-insensitive and tests whether the field contains the text.

notes.text: The source data lists this site as closed to the public, so do not enter or hunt here. If you think that is wrong, ask the managing body.
Pheasant and rabbit only, by a free lottery permit from the state. No deer or turkey hunting.
notes.sourceName: Illinois Department of Natural Resources, Gifford site page

notes.text: Pheasant and rabbit only, by a free lottery permit from the state. No deer or turkey hunting. This site crosses into Ford County, which has its own season rules.
notes.sourceName: Illinois Department of Natural Resources, Perdueville site page

notes.text: Hunting is not allowed. The district's rules also ban carrying a firearm or a bow on its land.
notes.sourceName: Champaign County Forest Preserve District, General Use Ordinance, section V

notes.text: No hunting without a district permit. The district runs an archery deer program by lottery at Rock Springs, Sand Creek, Friends Creek and Fort Daniel. Apply to the district.
notes.sourceName: Macon County Conservation District, Deer Herd Management Program

notes.text: State sites each have their own rules, and many small state sites are closed to hunting. Check this site on the state's list before you hunt.
notes.sourceName: Illinois Department of Natural Resources, public hunting areas, east central region

notes.text: This is private conservation land. Access and hunting need the owner's permission.

default.text: Open to the public does not mean open to hunting. Ask the managing body before you hunt here.
